title: CPU Optimization
description: Advanced techniques for optimizing CPU performance including undervolting, power limits, and thermal management for Intel and AMD processors.

prerequisites.title: Before You Begin
items: Create a system restore point before making any changes
Understand that improper settings can cause system instability
Have a stress testing tool ready (Prime95, AIDA64, Cinebench)

steps.title: Understanding CPU Optimization
steps.content:
CPU optimization involves balancing performance, power consumption, and thermals. Key concepts:

**Undervolting**
Reduces voltage supplied to CPU cores without reducing clock speed. Results in lower temperatures and potentially better sustained performance.

**Power Limits (PL1/PL2)**
PL1 = Sustained power limit (long-term)
PL2 = Boost power limit (short-term burst)
Adjusting these affects sustained vs. burst performance.

**Thermal Design Power (TDP)**
The amount of heat the cooling system is designed to dissipate. Higher TDP = more performance but more heat.

infoBox.title: Why Undervolt?
infoBox.content: Modern CPUs are often shipped with higher voltages than necessary for stability margin. Undervolting removes this excess, reducing heat without losing performance.

steps.title: Intel CPU Undervolting
steps.content:
Use Intel XTU or ThrottleStop for Intel processors.

**Intel XTU (Official Tool)**
1. Download from Intel's website
2. Launch Intel XTU
3. Go to "Core" section
4. Reduce "Core Voltage Offset" by -50mV
5. Click Apply

**ThrottleStop (Third-Party)**
1. Download from techpowerup.com
2. Launch ThrottleStop
3. Click "FIVR"
4. Select "CPU Core" and "CPU Cache"
5. Check "Unlock Adjustable Voltage"
6. Set Offset Voltage to -50mV
7. Click Apply and OK

**Testing Undervolt Stability:**
1. Run Prime95 for 30+ minutes
2. Monitor temperatures with HWiNFO64
3. If stable, increase undervolt by -10mV
4. Repeat until instability occurs
5. Back off to last stable value

infoBox.title: Stability Note
infoBox.content: If you experience crashes or blue screens, reduce the undervolt. Typical stable values range from -80mV to -150mV depending on your specific CPU.

steps.title: AMD Ryzen Optimization
steps.content:
Use Ryzen Controller or Ryzen Master for AMD processors.

**Ryzen Controller**
1. Download from GitHub
2. Launch Ryzen Controller
3. Adjust these settings for balanced optimization:
• Temperature Limit: 85-90°C
• STAPM Limit: 35-45W (adjust based on cooling)
• Fast Limit: 45-65W
• Slow Limit: 35-45W

**AMD Ryzen Master (Official)**
1. Download from AMD's website
2. Select "Manual" profile
3. Adjust PPT (Package Power Tracking)
4. Set TDC (Thermal Design Current)
5. Configure EDC (Electrical Design Current)
6. Apply and test stability

**Curve Optimizer (Zen 3+)**
Available in BIOS for Ryzen 5000+ series. Allows per-core voltage curve optimization for better efficiency.

steps.title: Process Priority Management
steps.content:
Optimize CPU priority for gaming:

**Manual Priority Adjustment:**
1. Open Task Manager while game is running
2. Go to "Details" tab
3. Find the game process
4. Right-click → Set priority → "High" (not Realtime)

**Automatic Priority with Process Lasso:**
1. Download Process Lasso
2. Right-click game process
3. Select CPU Priority → Always → High
4. Process Lasso will automatically apply this setting

**Recommended Priority Settings:**
• Games: High
• Discord/Voice Chat: Above Normal
• Browser during gaming: Below Normal
• Background apps: Low

infoBox.title: Never Use Realtime
infoBox.content: Never set any process to "Realtime" priority. This can cause system instability and potentially freeze your computer.

steps.title: CPU Affinity & Core Parking
steps.content:
Advanced CPU optimization techniques:

**CPU Affinity**
Assign specific CPU cores to applications:
1. Open Task Manager → Details tab
2. Right-click process → Set affinity
3. Select which cores the process can use

**Disable Core Parking (Performance Mode)**
Windows may "park" unused cores to save power. To disable:
1. Open Power Options → Change plan settings → Advanced
2. Processor power management → Minimum processor state: 100%

**High Performance Plan Tweaks:**
• Minimum processor state: 5-10%
• Maximum processor state: 100%
• System cooling policy: Active
• Processor performance boost mode: Aggressive

infoBox.title: Expected Results
infoBox.content: After CPU optimization, expect 5-15°C lower temperatures and more consistent frame rates due to reduced thermal throttling.
